Method of Attack: Injecting vulnerabilities into source code using Unicode control characters to reorder tokens at the encoding level
Using Unicode bidirectional override characters (Bidi controls) to display code differently to humans and compilers
Homoglyph attacks using visually similar characters to create different logic
Embedding control characters in comments and strings to reorder source code logic
Techniques including Early Returns, Commenting Out, and Stretched Strings to hide malicious code
Discoverer: Researchers from the University of Cambridge
Impacted Systems: Software projects written in C, C++, C#, JavaScript, Java, Rust, Go, and Python
Multiple code editors and web-based repositories
Attack Vector: Manipulation of source code file encoding using Unicode control characters
Supply-chain attacks via source code repositories
Indicators of Compromise: Use of Unicode bidirectional override characters (e.g., LRI, RLI)
Presence of homoglyph characters in source code
Proof-of-concept scripts on GitHub demonstrating Trojan Source attacks
